title: Chest Pain Triage Protocol
body: Chest pain assessment: Determine onset (sudden vs gradual), location (central, left-sided, radiating), character (sharp, dull, pressure, crushing), severity (0-10), and associated symptoms (shortness of breath, diaphoresis, nausea, dizziness). Ask about exertional vs rest onset. History of cardiac disease, hypertension, diabetes, smoking, or family cardiac history increases risk. Red flags: sudden crushing/pressure pain, radiation to left arm or jaw, associated diaphoresis, syncope, or dyspnea at rest. Any suspicion of acute coronary syndrome warrants immediate ER referral.
disposition_notes: Sudden onset with red flags → ER_NOW. Exertional chest pain resolving at rest → URGENT_CARE. Mild reproducible chest wall pain without red flags → SAME_DAY.
